summary.intent: Skip urllib3's per-request `load_verify_locations()` CA-bundle reload for the default `verify=True` path by sharing one module-level, pre-loaded `SSLContext` across all such connections, since that reload was measured as the dominant cost under highly concurrent HTTPS traffic.
summary.issue_fit: No originating issue; intent taken from the PR title/body and the four commit messages (spec-pr6667-packet). The stated goal (avoid redundant `load_verify_locations()` calls for verify=True) is met at the code level, but the same sharing mechanism introduces two independent regressions.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff reviewed (the only changed file, src/requests/adapters.py, in full, including unchanged surrounding lines for context); the installed urllib3==2.8.0 dependency's connection/SSL-context code was read to establish base-vs-head guarantees. Two scratch pytest checks were run at the pinned head (test_shared_ssl_context_cert.py, test_import_crash_repro.py); both mandatory candidates were independently verified by a fresh-context worker and confirmed. Existing focused SSL/TLS tests were run once (`-k "different_connection_pool or mtls"`); `test_different_connection_pool_for_tls_settings_verify_bundle_unexpired_cert` failed as pre-declared (fixture/OpenSSL mismatch, pre-existing). `test_different_connection_pool_for_mtls_settings` also failed, on its very first, unmodified `verify=False` line, before any code this diff touches runs; this is consistent with the same pre-existing fixture-certificate/OpenSSL-version mismatch and is not attributed to this change, though it was not one of the two failures pre-declared by the run policy.

findings.title: Don't hand the shared preloaded SSLContext to connections that also set a client certificate
findings.trigger: Two HTTPS requests in one process use the default `verify=True` together with a per-request client certificate (`cert=(certfile, keyfile)`), whether concurrently from different threads/Sessions or sequentially one after another.
findings.impact: `_urllib3_request_context()` puts the module-level singleton `_preloaded_ssl_context` into `pool_kwargs['ssl_context']` for every `verify=True` connection, and urllib3's `ssl_wrap_socket()` calls `context.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile)` directly on whatever `ssl_context` object it is given (installed urllib3==2.8.0, util/ssl_.py:429-433) before `wrap_socket()`. Because the singleton is shared process-wide, loading one connection's client certificate onto it can leak into, race with, or overwrite another connection's handshake -- including a later cert-less verify=True request silently inheriting a previous request's client identity, and the TLS-in-TLS/proxy path, which reaches the same code. Confirmed independently: two connections built via `HTTPAdapter._get_connection()` with different `cert=` tuples share the identical `.ssl_context` object (`is` identity) while their own `.cert_file` correctly differs. At the merge-base, `verify=True` never set `ssl_context`, so urllib3 always built a private, per-connection context (installed urllib3==2.8.0, connection.py:1031-1034), making this cross-connection mutation structurally impossible.
findings.change: In `_urllib3_request_context()`, only reuse `_preloaded_ssl_context` when there is no client certificate, e.g. change `elif verify is True:` to `elif verify is True and client_cert is None:` (src/requests/adapters.py:94), so any request supplying `cert=` gets a private context the way it did before this change, for both the direct-connect and TLS-in-TLS/proxy paths.

findings.title: Loading the default CA bundle at import time can crash `import requests`
findings.trigger: `DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH` (certifi's bundle path, sometimes patched by Linux distributions to a system trust-store path) is missing, unreadable, or malformed at the moment `requests`/`requests.adapters` is imported -- even in a process that never issues a `verify=True` request.
findings.impact: The module now calls `_preloaded_ssl_context.load_verify_locations(extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH))` unconditionally at import time (src/requests/adapters.py:75-78). At the merge-base, the equivalent CA-bundle existence check ran lazily inside `cert_verify()`, guarded by `if url.lower().startswith("https") and verify:`, and only fired when an actual HTTPS request was sent, raising a deliberate, actionable `OSError` ("Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle, invalid path: ..."). At head, that check was rewritten to only run `if verify is not True:`, so the friendly error is unreachable for the default `verify=True` case, while the new eager module-level call raises a raw, unhandled `FileNotFoundError`/`ssl.SSLError` at `import requests` time instead -- confirmed by an independently executed scratch test that monkeypatches the bundle path and observes the import itself fail.
findings.change: Guard the module-level `load_verify_locations()` call so a missing or broken default bundle does not crash import (e.g. try/except around it), and reproduce the historical friendly `OSError` lazily on the first `verify=True` request if the preload failed.
